body.p: The undersigned thanks Examiner Allred for review and consideration of the present Application. In response to the Office Action of September 29, 2024 ("Office Action"), the undersigned submits the present amendment and remarks ("Response").

Upon entry of the present amendment, claims 1-20 will be pending in this application. Claims 1, 5, 6, 8, 12, 13, 15, 17, 18, and 20 have been amended. No new matter is added. Based on the following remarks, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims.

Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor regards as the invention. Accordingly, claims 1, 5, 6, 8, 12, 13, 15, 17, 18, and 20 have been amended to address the issues noted in the Office Action. III. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 4 102 & 103

Claims 1-4, 8-11, 15-16, and 20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Patent No. 10,479,506 B1 to Colletti ("Colletti"). Claims 5, 12, and 17 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Colletti in view of U.S. Patent No. 11,291,306 B1 to Bergdoll et al. ("Bergdoll"). Claims 6-7, 13-14, and 18-19 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Colletti in view of U.S. Patent No. 6,260,903 B 1 to von der Heyde ("von der Heyde").

Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections and submits that all the pending claims are patentable. Nevertheless, strictly in the interest of advancing prosecution, Applicant has amended the claims to further distinguish the pending claims from the references cited in the Action. Accordingly, these rejections are now moot, as the Office has not had the opportunity to assess the claims as fully set forth herein and thus has not shown relevance of the current rejections to the claims as presented herein. Moreover, for at least the reasons set forth below, Applicant submits that none of the cited references, alone or in combination with each other or any other cited reference, anticipate or render obvious the subject matter recited in the claims presented herein. Applicant accordingly requests withdrawal of the rejections and allowance of the pending claims.

Claims 1, 8, and 15 have been amended to recite, in relevant part, an attachment mechanism that comprises "a first attachment member configured to engage a circumferential portion of an armrest of the adjacent passenger seats" (emphasis added).

Colletti fails to describe a first attachment member configured to engage a circumferential portion of an armrest. Colletti teaches a first attachment member (base of the housing 132) as having a top 136, back 138, and lateral walls 134 that form a box-shaped housing, and as described and shown in FIG. 2 of Colletti, the base of the housing 132 is attached to the rear end 116 of the armrest 112. Thus, due to its described shape and attachment location, the base of the housing 132 therefore cannot be configured to engage a circumferential portion of the armrest 116.

For at least these reasons, Colletti, separately or in combination with each other or any other cited reference, fails to anticipate or render obvious the subject matter of independent claims 1, 8, and 15. Claims 1, 8, and 15 are therefore allowable. As dependent claims 5, 6, 12, 13, 17, 18, and 20 depend directly or indirectly from claims 1, 8, and 15, they are also allowable at least based upon their dependency from allowable base claims 1, 8, and 15.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant believes all claims now pending in this application are in condition for allowance. The issuance of a formal Notice of Allowance at an early date is respectfully requested.

Except for the issue fees payable under 37 C.F.R. § 1.18, the Director is authorized to charge any additional fees during pendency of this application, including any required extension of time fees, or credit any overpayment to Deposit Account Number 20-1430.
